title: Tame loud workloads by granular credit policies and resize playbook
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary: During a high-traffic window on 2026-02-28 we observed a dedicated GPU cluster degrade for ~23 minutes due to several high-amplitude workloads hitting the same allocation. Symptoms were elevated tail latencies, LRU cache churn, and evictions of low-priority reservations. This ticket captures the post-incident follow-ups: a pragmatic playbook to (1) isolate noisy high-util workloads, (2) correct systemic reservation mis-sizing, and (3) implement a more granular elastic-credit (burst) policy with safety caps.

Root cause analysis: Three small teams (A, B, and an internal QA harness) launched concurrent full-sequence generation jobs that were configured with aggressive concurrency and no token caps. Our reservation sizing logic used a 95th-percentile traffic snapshot which missed a recent shift in sequence-length distribution; as a result reservations were oversized for some tenants and undersized for others. The existing burst token bucket applied globally per-tenant with a single refill rate, which allowed sudden large bursts to starve neighbors. Telemetry links: latency dashboard https://dash.internal/redwood/dedicated/latency/2026-02-28, eviction timeline https://dash.internal/redwood/evictions/2026-02-28. Incident timeline and on-call notes: https://confluence.redwood/internal/postmortems/dedicated-2026-02-28.

Decision summary: We will not immediately change reservation accounting algorithm (requires longer runway). Instead, we adopt a 2-phase approach: Phase A (short-term, 2 weeks): deploy per-pool soft-fencing for high-amplitude workloads, enable tenant-level conservative burst ceilings, and introduce a reservation audit job to flag mismatches. Phase B (medium-term, 6–10 weeks): revise reservation right-sizing to include sequence-length histograms, implement fractional reservations for ephemeral jobs, and replace global burst token bucket with hierarchical credit buckets (per-tenant and per-pool).

Trade-offs considered: aggressive throttling would reduce customer latency but harms throughput for latency-tolerant batched jobs; risk of false-positive noisy-workload identification if we rely solely on peak qps; adding per-request sampling increases tracing cost. We favor conservative defaults with opt-in aggressive containment for known noisy classes.

Artifacts and PRs: prototype soft-fence PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7342, reservation-audit job PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/pull/189, telemetry panel branch https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-dashboards/pull/21. See design doc for hierarchical credits: https://confluence.redwood/internal/design/hierarchical-credits.
acceptance_criteria: Soft-fence logic deployed to canary pool and validated under synthetic noisy workload without causing >2% increase in stable-tenant tail latency
Reservation audit runs daily and surfaces at least 95% of previously observed mis-sized reservations in staging and production within 48h
A conservative per-tenant burst ceiling is enabled cluster-wide with a rollout plan and rollback script
Telemetry dashboards show a reduction in eviction events during controlled noisy-workload tests
steps: Deploy soft-fence controller to canary pool (ENG-967890: step 1) — guardrails: dry-run flag and rate-limited enforcement
Run reservation-audit job in staging for 72h and collect mismatches; produce CSV of candidates for rightsizing
Implement per-tenant conservative burst ceiling (config flag burst_ceiling.enabled=true) and ship to 10% of pools
Add synthetic noisy-workload test to CI that exercises the soft-fence and verifies no eviction amplification
Collate results and propose reservation right-sizing algorithm update (histogram-aware) for Phase B
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha Kaur: Initial writeup after incident; flagged two urgent actions: deploy soft-fence and run reservation audit. Assigned to Miguel.
2026-03-03 — Miguel Santos: Spun up canary pool and validated deployment path; found a config race in allocation agent that prevents soft-fence from preempting bursts. Created PR #7342.
2026-03-05 — Priya Raman (PM): Reviewed tradeoffs; asked engineering to prioritize telemetry coverage so SLO impact can be quantified before mass rollout.

2026-03-07 — Miguel Santos: Soft-fence PR merged to canary; ran synthetic noisy job suite — eviction spikes reduced by ~68% in canary compared to control. Linked logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/canary/967890
2026-03-09 — SRE: Discovered reservation-audit job produced many small candidates for rightsizing; we will add heuristics to ignore <1% traffic tenants. Updated audit PR with filters.
2026-03-10 — Aisha Kaur: Coordinated release window for per-tenant burst ceiling (10% pools first). PM approved rollout. Next: plan Phase B design review by 2026-03-20.
